extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organisations, media researchers, policymakers, and anyone interested in news consumption trends
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and data summary of the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2022 presenting metrics and findings about how people access, perceive, and engage with news across 46 markets. Includes methodology, country-level data, thematic analyses (young audiences, trust, polarisation, climate coverage, email newsletters), and reuse/licensing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news (trust metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how much people trust news generally (e.g., 'Only 26% of Americans trust news generally, a 3-point decrease').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documents a fall in trust following last year’s positive bump and reports country-level trust figures. Use this as a core comparative indicator of public confidence in news across markets and over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in news / declining interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of audience interest in news; the report notes a 'declining interest in news.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track changes in stated interest over time to identify weakening connections between journalism and the public; use alongside engagement and avoidance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: News avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which people avoid the news (the report notes 'a rise in news avoidance' and examples such as '46% [in the UK] say they avoid the news sometimes or often').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat news avoidance as a behavioural indicator distinct from trust and interest; report country percentages and trends and consider demographic breakdowns (e.g., by age).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience polarisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which news audiences are polarised; the report explores 'Have news audiences become more polarised over time?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measures of partisan sorting, divergent trust or consumption patterns, and time-series comparison to assess polarisation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection with news brands among younger audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength of younger audiences' relationship with news brands (noted as 'Younger audiences have a weaker connection with news brands').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine brand loyalty, frequency of use, and cross-platform habits for younger cohorts; the report references a supplementary 'kaleidoscope' report tracking young people's relationships with news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforms and channels used to access news
rubrics_metrics.description: Which platforms and channels people use to access news (e.g., 'increasingly accessing the news via platforms such as TikTok'; 'India is a strongly mobile-focused market, with 72% accessing news through smartphones').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report platform-specific shares (social platforms, apps, websites, TikTok, email, etc.) and device usage (smartphone vs. desktop). Compare across countries and age groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing behaviour (social/email sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which people share news via social media or email (example: '65% share news via social or email' in South Africa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sharing rates as an engagement metric; disaggregate by platform and market to understand social propagation of news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of email newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance and role of email as a news channel (the report includes a feature 'The role of email news').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess newsletter reach, open/click behaviour where available, and the role of email in connecting audiences to news brands relative to social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to individual journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Which journalists people pay most attention to and why (topic covered in 'Which journalists people pay most attention to and why?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure prominence, trust, and influence of named journalists; include qualitative reasons for attention where survey items capture them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to topic-specific coverage (e.g., climate, Ukraine)
rubrics_metrics.description: How people access coverage of specific topics such as climate news or perceptions of coverage of Ukraine ('How people access climate news'; 'Perceptions of coverage of Ukraine').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report topic-specific consumption pathways, perceived adequacy/fairness of coverage, and differences across demographics and markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country and market comparative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Country-level and market-level data comparisons across dimensions (the site provides 'Country and market data' and an interactive to 'Build your own charts' comparing dimensions between or within countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the interactive data to compare metrics (trust, avoidance, platform usage, sharing, device use, etc.) across the 46 markets; present both absolute figures and trends over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey methodology and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Research method used: 'YouGov survey of over 93,000 online news consumers in 46 markets', 'Research was conducted by YouGov (and their partners) using an online questionnaire in January and February 2022.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that findings are based on an online YouGov questionnaire with the stated fieldwork window; consider mode, sample representativeness, timing, and country coverage when interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse and licensing policy (CC BY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproduction and reuse policy: 'This report can be reproduced under the Creative Commons licence CC BY. We encourage free, attributed, reuse of our text, data or charts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reusing text, data, or charts, provide attribution per CC BY requirements and follow any linked guidance; slide presentation and charts are available for reuse with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverables and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary outputs: PDF report download, executive summary, slide presentation with all charts, interactive country data, and a supplementary report on young people's relationships with news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided slides, PDF, and interactive data to extract metrics and visualisations; cite the relevant supplementary report (e.g., 'The kaleidoscope') when referencing youth-related analyses.
